Disclaimer: The data has been provided by the district officials of Vizianagaram via IITTNiF.

label: Cropping and Soil Profile, Sonipat, Haryana

The soil profile data includes information on essential nutrients and fertility levels, enabling informed decisions for soil health management and sustainable agricultural practices. The datasets also offer insights into crop yields for Kharif and Rabi seasons, facilitating the analysis of seasonal productivity and planning for crop rotation. These resources are valuable for optimizing fertilizer use, enhancing crop yield predictions, and ensuring sustainable land management practices.

label: Cropping and Soil Suitability, Kamrup Metropolitan District, Assam

The data includes information on cropping systems and land use/land cover types, providing insights into agricultural land utilization and crop distribution. It also includes cropping intensity, helping assess productivity and optimize land management. The resource group also includes rice-cultivated areas and marks regions left fallow in the Rabi season after Kharif paddy cultivation (rice fallow areas). Additionally, rice-fallow areas are classified based on soil moisture suitability during the Rabi season (November-February). This information supports efficient crop rotation planning, enhances rice production strategies, and assists in sustainable resource management, benefiting agricultural productivity and resilience. Disclaimer: This dataset is provided by Survey of India (SoI)

label: Soil Classification and Properties Dataset for India

The dataset includes essential attributes such as Soil_code, order, sub order, group, sub group, family texture, family mineral composition, family temperature, and series. These attributes define various physical and chemical properties of the soil, including texture, mineral composition, and temperature regime, along with soil classification information from broad categories (order) down to specific details (series). This resource is crucial for land use planning, environmental studies, and agricultural assessments and is available for Varanasi. Disclaimer: This dataset is provided by Survey of India (SoI)

label: Soil Datasets, India

The resource group consists of comprehensive soil attributes, including depth, surface texture, pH, drainage, and slope for 6 districts across India - Washim in Maharashtra, Vizianagaram in Andhra Pradesh, Kamrup metropolitan District in Assam, Gurugram and Sonipat in Haryana, Varanasi in UP. Each attribute is crucial for understanding soil characteristics and their implications on agricultural practices, construction projects, and environmental management. The non soil classes are classified into respective classes like settlements and waterbodies.

label: Soil Map of India

label: Forest cover data for India (2021)
desc: The resource group provides detailed forest cover information for selected districts in India, including Washim, Vizianagaram, Varanasi, Kamrup, and Gurugram. The data classifies forest cover based on tree canopy density, allowing for precise categorization of forest types across these regions. Classes include water bodies, non-forest areas, scrub lands with sparse vegetation (tree canopy density <10%), open forest (tree canopy density between 10% and 40%), moderately dense forest (tree canopy density between 40% and 70%), and very dense forest (tree canopy density >70%). This resource aids in monitoring and assessing forest coverage and density for effective land management and conservation efforts in these districts. Disclaimer: This dataset is provided by Survey of India (SoI).

label: Large Forest Fire Monitoring, India
desc: Forest fires, if undetected and not extinguished on time, may turn into large forest fires that cause wide spread destruction. such fires require extensive resources in terms of firefighting force, materials, equipment and other logistical support for containment. Timely information and tracking of such large forest fire (LFF) events helps in devising strategies for planning, resource mobilization for their effective containment, thereby minimizing losses to forests. Hence a satellite based automated system of monitoring LFF was developed and launched in 2019. The system uses SNPP-VIIRS sensor (375 m resolution) fire hotspot data. The resource groups consists of such LFF events in Kamrup Meteropolitan and Washim districts. Disclaimer: This dataset is provided by Survey of India (SoI).

label: Near Real-Time Forest Fire Monitoring, India
desc: Near real-time forest fire monitoring program initiated by FSI alerts State Forest Departments towards forest fire incidences detected by MODIS (Moderate Resolution Imaging Spectro-radiometer) sensor on-board Aqua and Terra Satellite of NASA and SNPP-VIIRS (Suomi National Polar-orbiting Partnership - Visible Infrared Imaging Radiometer Suite) sensor, at least six times in 24 hours. the fire hotspots detected by MODIS (1 km resolution) and SNPP-VIIRS (375 m resolution) sensors are received at Shadnagar Earth station (NRSC). Fire hotspots are automatically processed , leading to quick responses by the field teams in fire containment. The resource group consists of identified forest fire hotspots in districts like Gurugram, Kamrup Metropolitan, Vizianagaram and Washim. Disclaimer: This dataset is provided by Survey of India (SoI).

label: Agro Climatic Data of Bengaluru City, Karnataka
desc: Urban regions often experience the urban heat island effect, making them warmer than surrounding rural areas. Bengaluru, once known for its pleasant climate, now faces increasing temperatures due to climate change. Key factors include rising greenhouse gas emissions, loss of green cover, and rapid urbanization. To analyze these changes, a database was created encompassing precipitation (mm), land surface temperature (Â°C), and Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) for all wards within the BBMP. This data helps in understanding the relationship between temperature changes, precipitation patterns, and vegetation cover depletion in the city.

label: Agro Climatic Data of Gurugram, Haryana
desc: The resource group offers a comprehensive agroclimatic dataset of Gurugram district in Haryana, encompassing key environmental variables critical for understanding the dynamics of agricultural ecosystems. This dataset includes the Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) which provides insight into vegetation health and density, Precipitation (in mm) and Land Surface Temperature (in Â°C) which reflects the surface temperature of the earth features. This dataset allows for a multifaceted analysis of how climatic conditions influence agricultural zones, particularly in the context of global environmental changes. By studying the interplay between precipitation, temperature, and vegetation, researchers can better understand crop yield fluctuations, soil moisture dynamics, and the effects of drought or excessive rainfall on the land.

label: Mandal wise rainfall data, Vizianagaram, Andhra Pradesh
desc: The resource group contains comprehensive rainfall data for various Mandal (or sub districts) across multiple time periods, including seasonal and cumulative observations. The dataset is structured into key segments: Kharif (June to September, South West Monsoon) and Rabi (October to March) seasons, as well as specific months like April and May  (up to 31st May). For each period, the data includes actual rainfall, normal (expected) rainfall, deviation percentage from the norm, and the total number of rainy days. Additionally, cumulative rainfall data from is provided, summarizing the total actual and normal rainfall, overall deviation percentage, status (e.g., surplus, normal, or deficit), and total rainy days for the year. This organized structure enables tracking of rainfall trends, identifying deviations, and assessing the frequency of rainy days, making it valuable for agricultural planning, water resource management, and climate monitoring. label: Administrative Boundaries, Sirmaur, Himachal Pradesh
desc: The resource group consists of administrative boundaries and divisions in the parts of the Sirmaur district in Himachal Pradesh, mapped as a part of National Hydrology Project. The administrative dataset are inclusive of both demarcated and undemarcated boundaries. A demarcated boundary is a clearly defined and often physically marked boundary. It has specific, recognized, and often legal delineations. These boundaries are established through surveys, legal agreements, and physical markers such as fences, walls, or signposts. An undemarcated boundary is less clearly defined and lacks specific physical markers or legal recognition. These boundaries might be more abstract or conceptual, often relying on natural features, historical usage, or community consensus.

label: Orthoimagery, Varanasi, Uttar Pradesh.
desc: The orthorectified images provide a high-resolution, geometrically accurate view of the Varanasi landscape, ensuring that each pixel accurately corresponds to real-world coordinates. These orthoimages are processed from drone images collected in the month of october, 2024 for Varanasi. The ground sampling distance (GSD) of these images are less than 5 cms. Additionally Digital Elevation Model (DEM) and Point Cloud LAZ files are also available with the provider. The data collection is done block wise. Each block is divided into tiles and the polygon shows footprint of one of the tiles.  This approach not only facilitates a comprehensive mosaic of the entire study area but also enables focused analyses on specific regions within Varanasi, making it highly beneficial for applications in urban planning, environmental monitoring, and resource management. The resource group consists of an orthorectified image as STAC and corresponding footprint as a feature dataset

This structured approach helps in gaining insights into specific areas while also supporting comprehensive mapping of the entire region. The resource group includes a cloud-optimized orthorectified image and its corresponding footprint for enhanced spatial understanding.

label: Landslide Damage Assessment, Wayanad, Kerala
desc: In July 2024, the Wayanad district in Kerala experienced one of the most devastating landslides in India's history. Triggered by intense rainfall, the landslide occurred on July 30 and led to a massive debris flow, resulting in the tragic loss of at least 392 lives. The landslide produced an unprecedented debris flow of nearly six million cubic meters, stretching eight kilometers downhill, making it five times larger than the previous record-holder, the 1998 Malpa landslide in Uttarakhand. The event has been extensively studied, revealing that the landslide began as a rock slide and evolved into a debris flow, which was exacerbated by the region's geological conditions and weathered rocks.The affected area included villages, such as Mundakkai and Chooralamala that includes Iruvazhinji river. Asset damage include 507 buildings, 3 schools, 4 bridges (total length of 112 m) and road of length 8.38 km. The resource group provides geographical boundary of landslide events and the features mapped as damaged asset.

label: Land Use Land Cover Data (ESRI) from Sentinel 2 Imagery, India
desc: The resource group provides 10-meter resolution Land Use and Land Cover (LULC) data, mapped at the national scale. This dataset was generated using a deep learning model trained on more than 5 billion hand-labeled Sentinel-2 pixels collected from over 20,000 sites spanning all major global biomes. The model leverages six Sentinel-2 surface reflectance bands—visible blue, green, red, near-infrared, and two shortwave infrared bands. To produce the final LULC map, the model processes multi-temporal imagery acquired throughout the year, with the results composited into a single representative map. The classes include water, trees, flooded vegetation, crops, built area, bare ground, snow/ice, clouds, rangeland

label: Coastal Erosion Analysis along Shoreline of Tamil Nadu
desc: Coastal erosion, exacerbated by climate change and human activities, poses significant threats to ecosystems, infrastructure, and communities worldwide. Tamil Nadu, located along India's eastern coast and bordered by the Bay of Bengal, faces escalating challenges from coastal erosion. A study was performed to examine the coastal erosion dynamics and future forecasting in Tamil Nadu, using data from 1997 to 2023. Predictive modelling techniques were used to forecast future shoreline changes. The results aid in targeted mitigation and adaptation strategies, enhancing coastal resilience and sustainability in Tamil Nadu, and highlight the importance of interdisciplinary collaboration and community participation in addressing coastal erosion challenges. The resource group consists of shoreline changes mapped in the years - 1997, 2009, 2014, 2019, 2023 and the predicted coastal erosion regions in the year 2035 and 2045.

label: Water Distribution Network in Satna City
desc: Publishes information from water Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) system in Satna city, at an interval of 15 minutes. The SCADA system is a control system that collects and analyzes data in real time to help water systems operate more efficiently. Satna city operates two Water Treatment Plants (WTPs). Water flows from the main water reservoir (anicut) to these WTPs. The water is pumped from the anicut through the pump house (RWPH). MLD-40 receives water from RWPH-1, while MLD-18 receives water from RWPH-2, 3, and 4. At the WTPs, the water undergoes filtration and is then pumped to Overhead Tanks (OHTs). The WTPs are equipped with flow meters and analyzers.
